programme: APEX1(Ref-1)-gated, HDAC3-corepressed, ATF6/UPR-coupled RELA(NF-κB) inflammatory transcription: APEX1's redox function licenses RELA/p65 DNA binding, HDAC3-NCoR/SMRT complexes set the chromatin threshold for how much of that RELA programme (TNF, IL6, CXCL8, ICAM1, VCAM1, CCL5, BIRC3, FASLG) is expressed, and ATF6-driven ER-stress signalling feeds proteotoxic/ischemic stress into the same output.
role_in_a: In Huntington's Disease, mutant-huntingtin-associated proteotoxic stress engages the ATF6 arm of the UPR (29523177, 26752648: ATF6 derepression/inhibition of DREAM-ATF6 interaction is neuroprotective in HD mouse models) while RELA/p65 drives a documented cytokine and endocannabinoid transcriptional programme in HD models (24360910, 25757558), with HDAC3 inhibition ameliorating HD pathology in mice (27031333, 33679321, 22590724) consistent with HDAC3 normally restraining or shaping this output, and APEX1-dependent DNA-repair/redox capacity is reduced in HD patient material (27182645).
role_in_b: In Stroke, ischemia-reperfusion is a classic trigger for ER stress and ATF6 activation, which is protective in a permanent-occlusion mouse model (40259100); RELA/NF-κB drives the leukocyte/endothelial/astrocytic inflammatory response to ischemia across several models (42621097, 42196418, 21487414); HDAC3 targeting of microglia via nanoparticle delivery modulates post-stroke neuroinflammation (42677156); and APEX1's redox/DNA-repair duality is highlighted as multifaceted in the cardiovascular system (40243693), the tissue compartment most proximal to blood-based sampling here.
shared_axis: Both a proteotoxic insult (mutant HTT misfolding) and an ischemic insult (hypoxia-reperfusion) converge on the same stress-to-inflammation relay in circulating/myeloid cells: redox state (APEX1) and ER stress (ATF6) tune how much RELA-driven cytokine/adhesion-molecule transcription occurs, with HDAC3 corepressor complexes setting the ceiling on that response — so the two diseases would share this axis not because one causes the other but because both are systemic stressors that recruit the same peripheral-immune-activation machinery.
reasoning: Three of the four carrying factors (HDAC3, ATF6, RELA) have dedicated experimental citations placing them independently in both Huntington's Disease and Stroke, and the fourth (APEX1) is placed in HD directly and in a redox/cardiovascular context adjacent to stroke — satisfying 'supported' rather than 'established' because no retrieved paper studies HD and stroke together through this module. No single patient subgroup drives it (HDAC3 is concordant in 36/63, RELA the weakest carrier at 26/63, still well above single-view recurrence rates of 0.02–0.19), so support_strength is strong rather than moderate.
support: 27031333/33679321/22590724 — HDAC3 inhibition ameliorates pathology in HD mouse models; 42677156 — HDAC3-targeted nanoparticle delivery modulates microglial neuroinflammation after stroke; 29523177/26752648 — ATF6 derepression is neuroprotective in HD mouse models; 40259100 — ATF6 activation is beneficial after permanent cerebral ischemia; 24360910/25757558 — RELA/p65 regulates cytokine and microRNA transcription in HD mouse/cell models; 42621097/42196418/21487414 — RELA/NF-κB drives inflammatory gene expression in stroke/ischemia models; 27182645 — DNA-repair gene (including APEX1-pathway) downregulation in HD patient material; 40243693 — APEX1's redox-signalling role reviewed in the cardiovascular system.
how_to_falsify: In matched peripheral blood monocytes/leukocytes from HD and stroke patient cohorts, measure APEX1 redox activity, ATF6 nuclear cleavage, HDAC3-NCoR occupancy at RELA target promoters (ICAM1, IL6, VCAM1), and RELA DNA binding together; if RELA-driven cytokine induction occurs without co-variation in APEX1 redox activity, ATF6 activation, or HDAC3 promoter occupancy in either disease, the proposed coupling is wrong.
caveats: Both networks were built from blood only, so this describes a peripheral/circulating-immune-cell axis, not a claim about brain tissue. 63 patient-group comparisons come from only 4 independent cohort pairs, so apparent concordance counts overstate independent replication. Canonical blood/inflammatory master regulators (CEBPD, BCL6, FOS, SMAD3, STAT3, TCF7, RUNX2, BCL3, CEBPB, ETS1, KLF2) were removed as tissue-generic before ranking — RELA's survival is therefore notable, but the broader NF-κB partner context they would normally provide is invisible in this list. NFYC, ZBTB7B, PBX2, NCOA1, ARID3A, TRIM28, TP53 and BRCA1 all met the concordance bar (26–32/63) but are excluded here because no retrieved literature ties them into this specific redox/UPR/NF-κB story, or (TRIM28, TP53, BRCA1) their disease-specific citations point to unrelated functions (transposable elements, SNP association, Huntingtin-BRCA1 DNA repair) rather than this inflammatory module.
